 Mr. Suvendu Kumar Ray, Advocate
 -versus-
 B.K. Pandy, Sr. Manager H.R. .... Opposite

entities.text: High Court Of Orissa At Cuttack
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: THE CHIEF JUSTICE  MR. JUSTICE MURAHARI SRI RAMAN  ORDER Order No. 13.03.2024 01.
This matter is taken up through Hybrid mode.

2. In the present contempt petition filed in 2024, the petitioner has alleged violation of an order dated 02.08.2016 passed in W.P.(C) No.21144 of 2014 and a subsequent order dated 03.10.2023 passed in CONTC No.1353 of 2016.

3. Our attention has been drawn by learned Additional Government Advocate representing the opposite parties-contemnors to the order dated 03.10.2023 passed in CONTC No.1352 of 2016, it has been mentioned wherein that the order dated 27.09.2023 has been complied with.
The dispute relates to payment of compensation to the petitioner upon acquisition of land.
The Special Land Acquisition Officer, NTPC, Angul has opined that the land acquisition proceeding lapsed few years back.

Therefore, steps are being taken for fresh acquisition proposal in accordance with the provisions of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 (RFCTLA R&R Act, 2013).
4.

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 (RFCTLA R&R Act, 2013)
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: In our considered view, no case of deliberate violation of this Court's order is made out.

5. Be that as it may, learned counsel representing the NTPC has submitted that computation of the amount of compensation under the new Act has been made and the amount has accordingly been deposited with the Land Acquisition Officer for disbursement to the petitioner.

Bidyadhar Sahoo vs B.K. Pandy on 13 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/135616316/
1 6.

In such view of the matter, the contempt proceeding stands dropped as in the opinion of the Court that no willful non- compliance of this Court's order is made out in the facts and circumstances of the case.

Once the amount has been released by the NTPC for payment to the petitioner which is lying with the Special Land Acquisition Officer, the Court sees no reason why the said amount shall not be paid to the petitioner without any further delay.
7. Accordingly, the contempt case stands disposed of.
(Chakradhari Sharan Singh) Chief Justice (M.S.Raman) Judge Aswini/S.Behera Designation:
